A09.treatment: ORS oral — 5 mL/kg after each loose stool. Zinc (elemental) oral 10mg daily × 14 days in children <5y. Homemade SSS (3 tsp sugar + ½ tsp salt in 200 mL water) if ORS unavailable. Antibiotics NOT indicated unless dysentery or cholera.
A09.referral: Severe dehydration, bloody stools, altered consciousness, <2 months of age, SAM with dehydration.

A15.treatment: Intensive phase (2 months): RHZE (Rifampicin 150mg + Isoniazid 75mg + Pyrazinamide 400mg + Ethambutol 275mg) — weight-based daily. Continuation phase (4 months): RH (Rifampicin 150mg + Isoniazid 75mg). Notifiable condition.
A15.referral: Disseminated TB, unable to manage on ambulatory basis, DR-TB contacts.

A16.treatment: Intensive phase (2 months): RHZE weight-based daily. Continuation phase (4 months): RH. Notifiable condition.

A17.treatment: Intensive phase: RHZE for 2 months. Continuation phase: RH for 7–10 months (total 9–12 months for CNS TB). Corticosteroids (Prednisone 40mg daily, taper over 4–6 weeks) usually added by specialist. Notifiable condition.
A17.referral: All cases — refer urgently for specialist management and monitoring.

A18.treatment: Standard RHZE × 2 months → RH × 4 months for most extrapulmonary TB. Duration may extend to 9–12 months for bone, joint, or CNS involvement. Notifiable condition.
A18.referral: All suspected cases — refer for diagnostic confirmation and specialist management.

A19.treatment: RHZE × 2 months → RH × 4 months. Screen for TB meningitis. Notifiable condition.
A19.referral: All cases — urgent referral for specialist management.

A22.treatment: Cutaneous anthrax: Ciprofloxacin 500mg oral 12 hourly × 60 days. Doxycycline 100mg 12 hourly × 60 days as alternative. Notifiable condition.

A36.treatment: Diphtheria antitoxin IM/IV + Benzathine benzylpenicillin 1.2 MU IM single dose. Notifiable condition.
A36.referral: All cases — urgent referral for antitoxin and airway management.

A37.treatment: Azithromycin 10 mg/kg oral once daily × 5 days (children) OR 500mg daily × 5 days (adults). Notifiable condition.
A37.referral: Infants <6 months, respiratory distress, notifiable — refer.

A46.treatment: Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500mg oral 6 hourly × 10 days (adults) OR 250mg 6 hourly × 10 days (children). Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin 500mg daily × 5 days.

A54.treatment: Uncomplicated gonorrhoea: Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose + Azithromycin 1g oral single dose. Treat partners. Test for other STIs including HIV.
A54.referral: PID, disseminated infection, ophthalmia neonatorum, pregnancy.

A69.2.treatment: Doxycycline 100mg oral 12 hourly × 14–21 days (adults). Children <8y and pregnancy: Amoxicillin 500mg 8 hourly × 14–21 days.

A75.treatment: Doxycycline 100mg oral 12 hourly × 7 days (adults). Children: Azithromycin. Notifiable (epidemic typhus).

A78.treatment: Doxycycline 100mg oral 12 hourly × 14 days (adults). Pregnancy: Azithromycin 500mg daily × 5 days. Children <8y: Azithromycin 10 mg/kg daily × 5 days.

A90.treatment: Dengue fever: supportive care with paracetamol (avoid NSAIDs and aspirin due to bleeding risk). Encourage oral fluids. Monitor platelets. Notifiable.
A90.referral: Warning signs: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, plasma leakage, shock.

A91.treatment: Dengue haemorrhagic fever requires aggressive fluid resuscitation and inpatient care. Avoid NSAIDs/aspirin. Notifiable.

B15.treatment: Hepatitis A: supportive care, rest, hydration, avoid hepatotoxic medicines and alcohol. Usually self-limiting.

B16.treatment: Acute hepatitis B: supportive care. If chronic (HBsAg+ >6 months) with active disease: Tenofovir 300mg daily (specialist). Screen contacts, vaccinate.
B16.referral: Acute liver failure, chronic HBV with cirrhosis, HIV co-infection.

B18.treatment: Chronic viral hepatitis: Tenofovir 300mg daily for HBV. HCV: direct-acting antivirals (specialist only). Avoid alcohol. Monitor LFTs and viral load.

B20.treatment: TLD (Tenofovir 300mg + Lamivudine 300mg + Dolutegravir 50mg) — 1 tab once daily. Add Cotrimoxazole 160/800mg daily if CD4 <200. Screen for TB at every visit. Baseline: CD4, VL, creatinine, HBsAg.
B20.referral: Cryptococcal meningitis (defer ART 4–6 weeks), TB meningitis (defer 8 weeks), pregnancy complications.

B24.treatment: Unspecified HIV disease: initiate TLD (TDF+3TC+DTG) once daily. Add Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis if CD4 <200. Screen for TB, STIs, mental health.

B50.treatment: Uncomplicated: Artemether/lumefantrine 20/120mg with fatty food. Weight-based: >5–15kg 1 tab, >15–25kg 2 tabs, >25–35kg 3 tabs, >35kg 4 tabs. 1st dose immediately, 2nd after 8h, then 12 hourly × 2 days (6 doses). Notifiable.
B50.referral: Severe malaria, vomiting, children <2y, pregnancy, HIV co-infection.

B51.treatment: P. vivax malaria: Artemether/lumefantrine as per P. falciparum PLUS Primaquine 15mg daily × 14 days (after G6PD test) to prevent relapse. Notifiable.

B54.treatment: Unspecified malaria: Artemether/lumefantrine 20/120mg weight-based, 6 doses over 3 days with fatty food. Notifiable.

B86.treatment: Permethrin 5% topical — apply neck to feet overnight, wash off after 8–12h. Repeat after 7 days. Treat all household contacts simultaneously. Wash linen in hot water. Children <2 months: Benzyl benzoate 12.5% diluted.
B86.referral: Secondary bacterial infection, crusted (Norwegian) scabies, immunocompromised.

C50.treatment: Breast cancer: refer for staging and specialist oncology (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormonal therapy). Palliative care for advanced disease (see Chapter 22).

C53.treatment: Cervical cancer: refer for staging and specialist oncology. Prevention: HPV vaccine (Grade 5 girls), cervical screening from age 30. Palliative care if advanced.

C61.treatment: Prostate cancer: refer for staging and specialist oncology (surgery, radiotherapy, hormonal therapy). Palliative care if metastatic.
C61.referral: All suspected cases — refer for PSA, biopsy, staging.

C80.treatment: Malignancy without site specification: refer urgently for diagnostic workup and staging. Initiate palliative care if advanced.

D50.treatment: Adults: Ferrous sulfate 170mg (55mg elemental iron) oral 12 hourly with meals. OR Ferrous fumarate 200mg 12 hourly. Children <5y: Iron 1–2 mg/kg elemental iron 8 hourly. Continue 3 months after Hb normalises. Deworm: Mebendazole or Albendazole.
D50.referral: Unknown cause, symptomatic anaemia, Hb ≤7 g/dL, men and non-menstruating women.

D64.9.treatment: Unspecified anaemia: request FBC, iron studies, B12, folate. Treat cause. Iron therapy if iron deficiency. Consider HIV, TB, chronic disease.
D64.9.referral: Unknown cause, symptomatic, cardiac failure, signs of chronic disease.

E03.9.treatment: Levothyroxine 100mcg oral daily on empty stomach. If ischaemic heart disease risk: start 25mcg daily, increase by 25mcg every 4 weeks. Elderly: start 50mcg daily. Check TSH after 2–3 months, then annually.

E05.treatment: Thyrotoxicosis: refer to specialist. Carbimazole, methimazole, or propylthiouracil are specialist-initiated. Beta-blockers (Propranolol 40mg 8 hourly) for symptom control while awaiting specialist.

E10.treatment: Short-acting insulin SC 3 times daily 30 min before meals + intermediate-acting at bedtime. Total daily dose 0.6 units/kg — 40–50% basal, rest split equally before meals. Monitor BG 3–4 times daily. Target HbA1c <7%.
E10.referral: All patients — hospital level management required.

E11.9.treatment: Step 1: Metformin 500mg oral once daily with meals, titrate to max 850mg 8 hourly. Step 2: Add Glimepiride 1mg daily, titrate to max 6mg. Step 3: Add insulin (intermediate-acting 10 units at bedtime), stop sulphonylurea. Target HbA1c <7%.
E11.9.referral: Acidotic breathing, hyperglycaemia >25 mmol/L, gangrene, sudden vision deterioration, eGFR <30, pregnancy.

E11.6.treatment: Type 2 diabetes with complications: Metformin 500–850mg 8 hourly. Add Glimepiride 1–6mg daily or insulin (basal 10 units at bedtime). Manage complications (nephropathy, neuropathy, retinopathy). Target HbA1c <7%, BP <140/90, LDL <1.8.

E16.2.treatment: Hypoglycaemia: if conscious — oral sugar/glucose. If unconscious — Dextrose 10% IV 2–5 mL/kg (adults: 5 mL/kg), recheck after 15 min, may repeat. Maintain with 5–10% dextrose infusion. Thiamine 200mg IV/IM if alcoholic/malnourished.
E16.2.referral: All on oral hypoglycaemics, no recovery after treatment, children.

E40.treatment: Kwashiorkor (SAM with oedema): stabilisation with F-75 (100 kcal/kg/day in 8 feeds) for 2–7 days, then transition to F-100/RUTF. Give Amoxicillin 45 mg/kg 12 hourly. Vitamin A, multivitamins, zinc, potassium, magnesium. Do NOT give iron initially.
E40.referral: All complicated SAM — refer urgently. Stabilise first.

E43.treatment: Severe acute malnutrition: F-75 (100 kcal/kg/day) if complicated, or RUTF if uncomplicated SAM. Amoxicillin 45 mg/kg 12 hourly. Vitamin A, multivitamins, zinc, potassium, magnesium. Watch for hypoglycaemia and hypothermia.
E43.referral: All complicated SAM, <6 months, weight <4kg, oedema, refusing feeds.

E44.treatment: Moderate acute malnutrition: RUTF (Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food) — 1 sachet daily. Multivitamins, zinc, vitamin A every 6 months. Deworming. Follow up monthly.
E44.referral: No weight gain after 2 months, medical complications, SAM develops.

E55.treatment: Vitamin D deficiency: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 50,000 IU weekly × 6–8 weeks, then 1,000–2,000 IU daily maintenance. Calcium supplementation if dietary intake inadequate.
E55.referral: Rickets with fractures, hypocalcaemic seizures, malabsorption.

E66.treatment: Obesity: diet (reduce refined carbs, increase fibre/veg), exercise 30 min × 5/week, weight loss target 5–10%. Screen for diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia. Consider referral to dietician.

E86.treatment: Dehydration: assess severity. Mild: ORS oral 5 mL/kg after each loose stool. Moderate: ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours. Severe: Sodium chloride 0.9% IV (or Ringer's lactate) 20 mL/kg bolus, repeat as needed.
E86.referral: Severe dehydration, shock, unable to take oral fluids.

F10.treatment: Alcohol use disorder: Thiamine 300mg oral daily × 14 days. Withdrawal: Diazepam 10mg oral, then 5mg 6 hourly × 3 days, 5mg 12 hourly × 2 days, 5mg daily × 2 days. Counselling, motivational interviewing. Refer for rehab.
F10.referral: Seizures, delirium tremens, severe dependence, pregnancy, failed community detox.

F17.treatment: Tobacco use disorder: nicotine replacement therapy (patch/gum) + behavioural support. Varenicline or Bupropion as adjunct (specialist). Counselling at every visit.

F20.treatment: Schizophrenia: Haloperidol 1.5–5mg oral daily (adults) or 0.75mg 12 hourly (elderly). Once stabilised: Flupenthixol decanoate 10–40mg IM every 4 weeks OR Zuclopenthixol decanoate 100–400mg IM every 4 weeks. Monitor for EPSE — Orphenadrine 50mg 8 hourly if needed.
F20.referral: Poor social support, suicidal/homicidal risk, children, elderly, pregnancy, no response.

F31.treatment: Bipolar disorder: Lithium (specialist-initiated, target 0.6–0.8 mmol/L) OR Valproate (avoid in women of childbearing potential). Antipsychotics (Haloperidol, Risperidone) for acute mania. Do NOT start antidepressants without specialist.
F31.referral: All cases — refer for specialist confirmation and management.

F32.9.treatment: Fluoxetine 20mg oral alternate days × 2 weeks, then 20mg daily. Reassess after 4 weeks. Continue minimum 9 months after remission. If sedating required: Amitriptyline 25mg at night (max 150mg). Ask about suicidal ideation at every visit.
F32.9.referral: Suicidal ideation, psychotic features, bipolar, pregnancy, children, failure after 8 weeks.

F41.9.treatment: Fluoxetine 20mg oral alternate days × 2–4 weeks, then 20mg daily. Continue minimum 12 months. Acute panic: Diazepam 2.5–5mg oral short-term (max 10 days). Psychotherapy (CBT) preferred first-line if available.
F41.9.referral: Risk of harm, comorbid severe conditions, poor response, repeated panic attacks, children.

F43.1.treatment: PTSD: trauma-focused CBT is first-line. Add Fluoxetine 20mg daily if needed. Treat comorbid depression, anxiety, substance use. Consider Prazosin for nightmares (specialist).
F43.1.referral: Severe symptoms, comorbid substance use, suicidal ideation.

F70.treatment: Mild intellectual disability: supportive care, behavioural therapy, family education. Treat comorbid psychiatric and medical conditions. Consider anxiety, depression, epilepsy before psychosis. Refer for developmental and educational support.
F70.referral: For assessment, rehabilitation, placement if needed.

G40.treatment: Focal epilepsy: Lamotrigine (start 25mg daily, titrate every 2 weeks to 100–200mg daily) OR Carbamazepine 100mg 12 hourly. Generalised: Lamotrigine OR Levetiracetam 500mg 12 hourly. Women of childbearing potential: avoid valproate. Acute seizure: Midazolam buccal 0.5 mg/kg (children) OR Diazepam 10mg IV.
G40.referral: New onset, mixed seizure types, focal needing MRI, seizure-free on therapy ≥5 years.

G43.treatment: Migraine: Paracetamol 1g oral + Metoclopramide 10mg oral at onset. NSAID (Ibuprofen 400mg) if no relief. Prophylaxis if ≥4 attacks/month: Amitriptyline 25mg at night OR Propranolol 40mg 12 hourly.
G43.referral: Atypical presentation, sudden severe headache, neurological signs.

G44.2.treatment: Tension headache: Paracetamol 1g oral 4–6 hourly as needed (max 4g daily). Lifestyle: stress management, relaxation, sleep hygiene, exercise. Exclude medication-overuse headache.
G44.2.referral: New headache >1 week, neurological signs, chronic >1 month no improvement.

G47.0.treatment: Insomnia: sleep hygiene (fixed wake time, no screens 1h before bed, no caffeine after 2pm), CBT-I. Short-term: Chlorphenamine 4mg at night (max 2 weeks). Avoid benzodiazepines long-term.
G47.0.referral: Chronic insomnia, suspected sleep apnoea, depression.

H10.treatment: Bacterial conjunctivitis: Chloramphenicol 1% ophthalmic ointment 6 hourly × 7 days. Viral: supportive (Oxymetazoline drops for redness). Allergic: Sodium cromoglycate 2% drops + Cetirizine 10mg daily.
H10.referral: No response in 5 days, unilateral, vision loss, pupil irregularity, corneal haziness, gonococcal.

H25.treatment: Senile cataract: no medical treatment. Refer for surgical assessment. Manage reversible causes (diabetes, hypertension). Provide spectacles for refractive error.

H40.treatment: Chronic open-angle glaucoma: Timolol 0.5% eye drops 12 hourly (specialist-initiated). Acute closed-angle glaucoma: Acetazolamide 500mg oral immediately, then 250mg 6 hourly. Pilocarpine 2% drops. Urgent referral.
H40.referral: All cases — ophthalmologist. Acute: within 12 hours.

H54.treatment: Blindness/low vision: refer for low vision assessment, spectacles, magnifiers, orientation and mobility training. Address reversible causes. Register with Department of Social Development for disability grant.

H60.treatment: Otitis externa: Acetic acid 2% in alcohol 3–4 drops into ear 6 hourly × 5 days after cleaning. Furuncular: Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days OR Flucloxacillin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days. Keep ear dry.
H60.referral: No response, severe pain, systemic symptoms, diabetic patient.

H65.treatment: Non-suppurative otitis media (with effusion): often self-limiting. Treat allergic rhinitis (Cetirizine 10mg daily). Valsalva, autoinflation. Reassess in 3 months.
H65.referral: Persistent >3 months, hearing loss, speech delay, structural abnormalities.

H66.treatment: Acute otitis media: Amoxicillin 45 mg/kg 12 hourly × 5 days (children). Adults: Amoxicillin 1500mg 12 hourly × 5 days. If amoxicillin in last 30 days: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid. Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin 10 mg/kg daily × 3 days.
H66.referral: No response after 72 hours, recurrent, mastoid swelling, suspected meningitis.

H81.treatment: Vertigo: Betahistine 16mg oral 8 hourly (or 8mg 8 hourly). Acute: Prochlorperazine 5mg oral 8 hourly. Vestibular rehabilitation exercises. Exclude central causes.
H81.referral: Atypical presentation, neurological signs, hearing loss, persistent >4 weeks.

I10.treatment: Step 1: Lifestyle — salt restriction, weight loss, exercise 30 min × 5/week, stop smoking. Step 2: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily. Step 3: Add Amlodipine 5mg daily OR Enalapril 10mg daily. Titrate monthly. Target BP <140/90 mmHg.
I10.referral: Young adults <30y, pregnancy, uncontrolled on 4 medicines, signs of organ damage, hypertensive emergency.

I11.9.treatment: Hypertensive heart disease without failure: Lifestyle modification + Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily + Enalapril 10mg daily. Target BP <140/90. Add Aspirin 150mg daily if secondary prevention indicated. Statin if 10-year CVD risk ≥20%.
I11.9.referral: Heart failure develops, poor control, LVH on ECG.

I15.9.treatment: Secondary hypertension: investigate cause (renal, endocrine, drugs). Treat underlying condition. Antihypertensives as for primary hypertension if needed. Specialist referral for workup.
I15.9.referral: All cases — specialist for investigation and management.

I20.treatment: Stable angina: Aspirin 150mg daily. Beta-blocker (Atenolol 50mg daily, titrate to HR ~60). Nitrate (Isosorbide dinitrate 5mg SL for attacks). Statin (Rosuvastatin 10mg at night). If still symptomatic: add Amlodipine 5mg daily. Then Isosorbide mononitrate 10–20mg BD.
I20.referral: Unstable angina, poor control, diagnostic uncertainty.

I21.treatment: Acute MI: Aspirin 150mg chewed. Isosorbide dinitrate 5mg SL. Morphine 5–10mg slow IV. Streptokinase 1.5 million units IV over 30–60 min if within 12 hours and no contraindications. Refer URGENTLY.
I21.referral: All cases — urgent transfer to hospital.

I25.treatment: Chronic ischaemic heart disease: Aspirin 150mg daily. Statin (Rosuvastatin 10mg at night). Beta-blocker (Atenolol 50mg daily). ACE-inhibitor (Enalapril 5–10mg BD). Nitrate as needed. Lifestyle modification.
I25.referral: Unstable symptoms, heart failure, poor control.

I48.treatment: Atrial fibrillation: rate control with Beta-blocker (Atenolol 50mg daily) OR Digoxin (specialist). Anticoagulation (Warfarin or DOAC — specialist). Treat underlying cause. Assess CHA2DS2-VASc score.
I48.referral: All cases — specialist for anticoagulation decision.

I50.treatment: Furosemide 40mg oral daily (titrate to effect, max 80mg BD). Enalapril 2.5mg 12 hourly, titrate to 10mg twice daily. Add Carvedilol 3.125mg twice daily after ACE-inhibitor stabilised, titrate every 2 weeks. Add Spironolactone 25mg daily if still symptomatic.
I50.referral: All suspected cases for initiation of treatment, poor response, prosthetic valve, suspected endocarditis.

I63.treatment: Ischaemic stroke: Aspirin 300mg oral as pre-referral dose (if able to swallow, no haemorrhagic signs). Do NOT treat elevated BP at PHC. Nil per mouth until swallowing assessed. Refer URGENTLY (preferably within 3 hours).

I64.treatment: Stroke unspecified: Aspirin 300mg oral pre-referral if not haemorrhagic. Nil per mouth. Refer URGENTLY.

I80.treatment: DVT: Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC 12 hourly OR Warfarin (target INR 2–3, specialist). Continue 3–6 months. Compression stockings. Investigate cause.
I80.referral: All suspected DVT — refer for confirmation and anticoagulation initiation.

I83.treatment: Varicose veins: compression stockings (30–40 mmHg). Elevation. Avoid prolonged standing. Refer if symptomatic, skin changes, ulceration.
I83.referral: Ulceration, bleeding, severe symptoms, cosmetic concern.

I84.treatment: Haemorrhoids: high fibre diet, hydration, avoid straining. Lactulose 10–20 mL daily. Topical Bismuth subgallate ointment. Lidocaine 2% cream for pain. Sitz baths.
I84.referral: Thrombosed, irreducible, bleeding, poor response, children.

I95.treatment: Hypotension: identify cause (dehydration, sepsis, cardiac, medication). If symptomatic: Sodium chloride 0.9% IV. If drug-induced (antihypertensives): adjust dose. Adrenal insufficiency: Hydrocortisone.
I95.referral: Shock, syncope, chest pain, suspected cardiac cause.

J00.treatment: Common cold: rest, hydration, Sodium chloride 0.9% nose drops (infants). Paracetamol 15 mg/kg (children) or 1g (adults) 6 hourly for fever/discomfort. No antibiotics. Reassess if symptoms >14 days.

J01.treatment: Acute sinusitis: Amoxicillin 500mg oral 8 hourly × 5 days (children ≤3y: 45 mg/kg 12 hourly). Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin 500mg daily × 3 days. Add Oxymetazoline 0.05% nose drops (max 5 days). Saline nasal irrigation.
J01.referral: Fever >48h, poor response >5 days, periorbital cellulitis, recurrent, meningeal signs.

J02.treatment: Acute pharyngitis (sore throat): salt water gargles (2.5 mL salt in 200 mL warm water). Paracetamol for pain. Antibiotics only if streptococcal risk (age 3–21y with enlarged tonsils + no cough + exudates): Benzathine benzylpenicillin 1.2 MU IM single dose OR Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg daily × 10 days.
J02.referral: Suppurative complications, recurrent (≥6/year), suspected rheumatic fever, difficulty opening mouth.

J03.treatment: Acute tonsillitis: same as J02 — antibiotics only if streptococcal risk. Benzathine benzylpenicillin 1.2 MU IM single dose (children ≥30kg and adults) OR 600,000 IU (<30kg). OR Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg daily × 10 days. Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin.
J03.referral: Peritonsillar/retropharyngeal abscess, trismus, recurrent, suspected rheumatic fever.

J04.treatment: Acute laryngitis and tracheitis: rest voice, hydration, humidifier. Paracetamol for pain/fever. Antibiotics not usually indicated.

J06.9.treatment: Acute URTI: rest, hydration, Paracetamol for fever/pain. Saline nose drops for infants. Antibiotics not indicated for viral URTI.
J06.9.referral: Symptoms >14 days, complications (otitis media, sinusitis, pneumonia).

J18.9.treatment: Uncomplicated: Amoxicillin 1g oral 8 hourly × 5 days. Severe penicillin allergy: Moxifloxacin 400mg daily × 5 days. With comorbidities/>65y: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 875/125mg 12 hourly × 5 days. Chest X-ray, sputum for TB-NAAT.
J18.9.referral: Confusion, cyanosis, RR ≥30, SBP <90, no response after 48h, comorbidities.

J30.treatment: Allergic rhinitis: Fluticasone nasal spray 100mcg each nostril 12 hourly. If no response in 7 days: Sodium cromoglycate 2% eye drops for eye symptoms. Add Cetirizine 10mg daily for long-term. Avoid sedation-causing antihistamines in children <2y.
J30.referral: Chronic symptoms, severe, patients on protease inhibitors requiring steroids.

J40.treatment: Bronchitis: usually viral, antibiotics not indicated. Paracetamol for fever/pain. Salbutamol inhaler if wheeze. Reassess if not improving in 1 week.
J40.referral: Symptoms >3 weeks, haemoptysis, weight loss, suspected pneumonia.

J45.treatment: Step 1: Salbutamol MDI 200mcg as needed. Step 2: Budesonide 200mcg 12 hourly. Step 3: Salmeterol/Fluticasone 50/250mcg 12 hourly. Acute: Prednisone 40mg daily × 7 days. Use spacer for all inhalers.
J45.referral: Children <6y, brittle asthma, >2 prednisone courses in 6 months, poor control on Step 2–3.

J45.9.treatment: Asthma: Salbutamol 100mcg MDI 200mcg (2 puffs) as needed. Add Budesonide 200mcg 12 hourly if using SABA >2×/week. Step-up as per J45.

J44.treatment: COPD: Salbutamol 100mcg MDI 1–2 puffs 3–4× daily as needed. If uncontrolled: Formoterol 12mcg 12 hourly. Frequent exacerbations (≥2/year) with eosinophils >0.1: Salmeterol/Fluticasone 50/250mcg 12 hourly. Influenza vaccine annually. Smoking cessation.
J44.referral: Poor response, patients on protease inhibitors requiring ICS.

J90.treatment: Pleural effusion: diagnose cause (TB, malignancy, cardiac failure, pneumonia). Treat underlying condition. Therapeutic aspiration if large. TB pleural effusion: RHZE × 2 months → RH × 4 months + corticosteroids.
J90.referral: All cases — refer for diagnostic workup.

K02.treatment: Dental caries: refer to dentist/dental therapist. Paracetamol for pain. Oral hygiene education. Lidocaine 2% with adrenaline for dental procedures (dentist).

K04.treatment: Pulp/periapical disease: refer to dentist. Paracetamol for pain. Root canal or extraction by dentist.

K05.treatment: Gingivitis: oral hygiene (brush 2× daily, floss, salt mouthwash). Chlorhexidine 0.2% mouthwash 15 mL twice daily × 5 days. Periodontitis: same + refer for scaling. Necrotising: Metronidazole 400mg 8 hourly × 5 days + Chlorhexidine.

K21.treatment: GERD: Pantoprazole 40mg oral daily for max 14 days. Lifestyle: stop smoking, small frequent meals, avoid late meals, weight loss, elevate head of bed. Stop NSAIDs if possible.
K21.referral: Weight loss, anaemia, persistent vomiting, haematemesis, dysphagia, palpable mass, no response in 7 days.

K25.treatment: Gastric ulcer: Pantoprazole 40mg daily × 8 weeks. If H. pylori positive: triple therapy — Pantoprazole 40mg 12 hourly + Amoxicillin 1g 12 hourly + Clarithromycin 500mg 12 hourly × 14 days. Stop NSAIDs, stop smoking.
K25.referral: Bleeding, perforation, obstruction, no healing after 8 weeks.

K27.treatment: Peptic ulcer: Pantoprazole 40mg oral daily × 4–8 weeks. H. pylori eradication if positive. Stop NSAIDs/smoking. Antacids for breakthrough symptoms.
K27.referral: Bleeding (haematemesis, melaena), perforation, obstruction, poor response.

K29.treatment: Gastritis/duodenitis: Pantoprazole 40mg daily × 4 weeks. Antacids (Aluminium/Magnesium hydroxide) for breakthrough symptoms. Avoid NSAIDs, alcohol, spicy food, smoking.
K29.referral: Bleeding, weight loss, persistent vomiting, poor response.

K30.treatment: Functional dyspepsia: Pantoprazole 40mg daily × 4 weeks. Lifestyle: small frequent meals, avoid triggers. Reassure (no serious pathology). If no response, refer to exclude organic disease.
K30.referral: Warning signs (weight loss, anaemia, vomiting, dysphagia), no response in 4 weeks.

K35.treatment: Acute appendicitis: keep nil per mouth, IV Sodium chloride 0.9%, analgesia (Morphine 5–10mg IM if severe). Refer URGENTLY for surgical assessment.

K40.treatment: Inguinal hernia: refer for surgical repair. If incarcerated/strangulated: urgent referral. Advise avoiding straining/heavy lifting.
K40.referral: All cases — surgical. Urgent if incarcerated.

K42.treatment: Umbilical hernia: refer for surgical repair if symptomatic or >2 cm. In children <2y, may resolve spontaneously.

K52.9.treatment: Non-infective gastroenteritis: hydration (ORS). Loperamide 4mg then 2mg after each loose stool (adults). Avoid lactose, caffeine, alcohol. Reassess if >4 weeks.
K52.9.referral: Blood in stool, weight loss, symptoms >4 weeks, dehydration.

K59.0.treatment: Constipation: high fibre diet, hydration, exercise, regular bowel habits. Lactulose 10–20 mL daily (adults) or 0.5 mL/kg (children). Sennosides 13.5mg at night if needed.
K59.0.referral: Recent change in bowel habit, faecal impaction, poor response.

K76.0.treatment: Fatty liver: weight loss 7–10%, exercise, avoid alcohol, control diabetes/lipids. Investigate for metabolic syndrome. No specific medicine.
K76.0.referral: Elevated LFTs, cirrhosis signs, metabolic complications.

K80.treatment: Gallstones: if asymptomatic — no treatment. Symptomatic: analgesia (Morphine 5–10mg IM for severe colic). Refer for cholecystectomy.

L01.treatment: Impetigo: Povidone iodine 5% cream 8 hourly. If extensive/systemic: Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days OR Flucloxacillin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days. Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin.
L01.referral: No improvement after 2nd course, haematuria (post-strep GN).

L02.treatment: Boil/abscess: incision and drainage is primary treatment. Antibiotics only if: extensive cellulitis, fever, face boils, immunocompromised, diabetic, neonate. Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days OR Flucloxacillin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days.
L02.referral: Palm/pulp space abscess, severe sepsis, deep abscess, poor response.

L03.treatment: Cellulitis: Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days OR Flucloxacillin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days. Elevate limb. Severe penicillin allergy: Azithromycin. Severe cellulitis: refer for IV antibiotics.
L03.referral: Significant pain/swelling (children), haemorrhagic bullae, gangrene, systemic symptoms, hand/face/scalp involvement, diabetic.

L08.9.treatment: Local skin infection: Povidone iodine 5% cream. If spreading or systemic: Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days. Keep clean and dry.

L20.treatment: Atopic eczema: Emollient (Emulsifying ointment) + Aqueous cream as soap substitute. Step 2: Hydrocortisone 1% topical 12 hourly × 7 days. Step 3: Betamethasone 0.1% (potent) for severe (avoid face). Itch: Chlorphenamine 4mg at night (max 2 weeks) or Cetirizine 10mg daily.
L20.referral: No improvement in 2 weeks, extensive, eczema herpeticum, infants needing >1% hydrocortisone.

L30.9.treatment: Dermatitis: emollient + topical hydrocortisone 1% 12 hourly × 7 days. Antihistamine for itch. Avoid triggers.

L40.treatment: Psoriasis: Coal tar (LPC 5%) topical 1–4× daily. Betamethasone 0.1% topical 12 hourly (potent). Sun exposure. For severe: refer for methotrexate/biologicals.
L40.referral: Severe, joint involvement, HIV-related, no response.

L50.treatment: Urticaria: avoid triggers. Chlorphenamine 4mg oral 6–8 hourly (adults) or 0.1 mg/kg (children). Cetirizine 10mg daily for long-term. Calamine lotion topically. DO NOT use oral corticosteroids.

L60.treatment: Nail disorders: depends on cause. Fungal: Fluconazole 200mg weekly × 6 weeks (adults). Trauma: no treatment. Psoriatic: treat psoriasis. Ingrown: warm soaks, avoid tight shoes.

L81.treatment: Pigmentation disorders: sun protection (SPF 30+), cosmetic camouflage. Vitiligo: high potency sunblock, moderate sun exposure. Albinism: SPF 30+, protective clothing, sunglasses.
L81.referral: All albinism, vitiligo for specialist, suspected malignancy.

M15.treatment: Polyarthrosis: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly (max 4g/day) + methyl salicylate ointment. Exercise, weight loss, physiotherapy. Add Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly if inflammation (max 7 days).
M15.referral: Intractable pain, joint replacement consideration, uncertain diagnosis.

M17.treatment: Knee osteoarthritis: Paracetamol + exercise + weight loss. Physiotherapy. Walking stick. Ibuprofen short course if inflamed. Intra-articular steroid injection (specialist).

M19.9.treatment: Arthrosis: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly + Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly (short course). Exercise, weight loss, physiotherapy.

M25.5.treatment: Joint pain: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly. Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly with meals if inflamed. Heat/ice. Rest and exercise.
M25.5.referral: Pain >1 week (children), >2 weeks (adults), fever, systemic illness.

M54.5.treatment: Low back pain: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly. Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly if muscle spasm. Avoid bed rest — stay active. Physiotherapy. Weight loss.
M54.5.referral: Neurological signs (numbness, weakness, bladder/bowel loss), red flags (weight loss, cancer history, age >50 with new pain).

M75.1.treatment: Rotator cuff syndrome: rest, ice, Paracetamol, NSAID (Ibuprofen). Physiotherapy with range-of-motion and strengthening. Subacromial steroid injection (specialist).

M79.1.treatment: Myalgia: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly. Heat. Rest. Hydration. Treat underlying cause (viral, medication, thyroid).
M79.1.referral: Persistent >2 weeks, weakness, systemic symptoms, rhabdomyolysis.

N30.treatment: Cystitis: Gentamicin IM 160mg single dose OR Fosfomycin 3g single dose OR Nitrofurantoin 100mg 6 hourly × 5 days (pregnancy-safe). Increase oral fluids. Send MSU for MC&S.
N30.referral: Pregnant, men, women beyond reproductive age, recurrent, sepsis.

N39.0.treatment: UTI: Uncomplicated: Gentamicin IM 160mg single dose. Complicated: Ciprofloxacin 500mg 12 hourly × 7 days. Pregnancy: Fosfomycin 3g single dose OR Nitrofurantoin 100mg 6 hourly × 5 days.
N39.0.referral: Pregnancy, men, children ≤3 months, sepsis, recurrent.

N18.treatment: CKD: Enalapril 5mg 12 hourly (titrate to 10mg 12 hourly) to reduce proteinuria. BP target <140/90. Statin if indicated. Avoid nephrotoxics (NSAIDs, tenofovir). Furosemide 20–80mg for fluid overload. Monitor K+ and creatinine.
N18.referral: eGFR <60, uncontrolled BP, hyperkalaemia, anaemia, dialysis consideration.

N20.treatment: Kidney stones: Morphine 5–10mg IM for severe colic. Hydration (2–3 L/day). Strain urine for stone analysis. NSAIDs contraindicated (renal risk). Refer for urology.
N20.referral: All <19 years, pregnant, morbidly obese, polycystic kidney disease, metabolic disorders, multiple stones, recurrent.

N40.treatment: BPH: refer for urology assessment. Urinary retention: insert urethral catheter, refer urgently. Avoid anticholinergics and decongestants.
N40.referral: All suspected BPH — refer for assessment.

N80.treatment: Endometriosis: NSAID (Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly) for pain. Combined oral contraceptive for symptom control. GnRH analogues (specialist). Refer for surgical assessment.

N91.treatment: Amenorrhoea: exclude pregnancy, thyroid, hyperprolactinaemia, PCOS. Lifestyle (weight, exercise). Combined oral contraceptive for cycle regulation. Refer for specialist workup.
N91.referral: Primary amenorrhoea >16y, secondary >6 months, suspected PCOS, infertility.

N92.treatment: Menorrhagia: Combined oral contraceptive (30mcg EE) × 3–6 months. Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly during menses. Ferrous sulfate if anaemic. Tranexamic acid 1g 8 hourly during menses.
N92.referral: Severe anaemia, suspected fibroids, no response, >45y with new bleeding.

O10.treatment: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy: Methyldopa 250mg 8 hourly, titrate to max 750mg 8 hourly. Do NOT use ACE-inhibitors, ARBs, or thiazides. Baseline bloods, urine protein. Refer for specialist antenatal care.

O13.treatment: Gestational hypertension (no severe features): Methyldopa 250mg 8 hourly, titrate. Weekly BP + urine protein + fetal monitoring. Education on warning signs.
O13.referral: Severe features (BP >160/110, symptoms, abnormal labs) — urgent referral.

O14.treatment: Pre-eclampsia without severe features: admit/monitor. With severe features: Magnesium sulfate 4g IV loading over 20 min + 10g IM (5g each buttock), then 5g IM every 4 hours. Nifedipine 10mg oral for BP ≥160/110. Insert Foley, monitor urine output hourly.
O14.referral: All cases — urgent referral to high-risk obstetric unit.

O15.treatment: Eclampsia: Magnesium sulfate 4g IV loading + 10g IM, then 5g IM every 4 hours. Left lateral position. Oxygen. Nifedipine for BP. Calcium gluconate 10% IV if magnesium toxicity (respiratory depression).
O15.referral: All cases — urgent transfer to high-risk obstetric unit.

O20.treatment: Bleeding in early pregnancy: monitor vitals, IV fluids if shock. Anti-D immunoglobulin 50mcg IM within 72h for Rh-negative women (surgical management).
O20.referral: All cases — urgent assessment to exclude ectopic/miscarriage.

O24.treatment: Diabetes in pregnancy: insulin is first-line (metformin may be added by specialist). Target fasting <5.3 mmol/L, 1h post-meal <7.8. Close monitoring of fetal growth. Refer to combined obstetric/diabetes clinic.

O80.treatment: Normal delivery: monitor partogram. Oxytocin 10 units IM after delivery (PPH prevention). Vitamin K 1mg IM for neonate. Chloramphenicol eye ointment for neonate. Delayed cord clamping (1 min).
O80.referral: Prolonged labour, fetal distress, PPH, retained placenta.

P07.treatment: Low birth weight: kangaroo mother care, exclusive breastfeeding (or expressed breastmilk). Monitor weight, temperature, glucose. Vitamin K 1mg IM at birth. Refer if <1.5kg or unstable.

P59.treatment: Neonatal jaundice: assess level (transcutaneous or serum bilirubin). Phototherapy if above treatment threshold. Ensure adequate feeding (breastfeed 8–12× daily). Exclude haemolytic causes.
P59.referral: Jaundice <24h of life, jaundice >2 weeks, bilirubin near exchange threshold, pallor, poor feeding.

R05.treatment: Cough: identify and treat cause. Viral URTI: supportive. Post-infectious: honey, fluids. If >3 weeks: exclude TB, asthma, post-nasal drip, GORD. Avoid cough suppressants in children.
R05.referral: Chronic cough >3 weeks, haemoptysis, weight loss, dyspnoea.

R07.4.treatment: Chest pain: exclude life-threatening causes (ACS, PE, aortic dissection, pneumothorax). If suspected ACS: Aspirin 150mg chewed, nitrates SL, urgent referral. ECG.
R07.4.referral: All suspected ACS, PE, aortic dissection — urgent.

R10.treatment: Abdominal pain: history + examination to exclude surgical abdomen. If renal/biliary colic: Morphine 5–10mg IM. Hyoscine butylbromide 10mg 6 hourly for cramps (max 3 days).
R10.referral: Severe pain, acute abdomen, bloody stools, mass, non-diarrhoeal bleeding.

R11.treatment: Nausea/vomiting: hydration. Children: ORS small frequent volumes. Adults: Metoclopramide 10mg oral/IM 8 hourly. Exclude pregnancy.
R11.referral: Severe dehydration, shock, jaundice, sepsis signs, projectile vomiting (infants), blood in vomit.

R42.treatment: Dizziness: exclude serious causes (stroke, cardiac arrhythmia, vertigo). If vertigo: Betahistine 16mg 8 hourly. Prochlorperazine 5mg oral for acute vertigo.
R42.referral: New focal neurology, cardiac cause, syncope.

R50.treatment: Fever: identify cause. Paracetamol 15 mg/kg (children) or 1g (adults) 6 hourly for distress. Hydration. Test for malaria if in endemic area. No empirical antibiotics (except infants <2 months with severe features).
R50.referral: Fever >2 days with no cause, warning signs (meningitis, sepsis, malaria), infants <2 months.

R51.treatment: Headache: Paracetamol 1g 4–6 hourly. Exclude serious causes (meningitis, SAH, tumour, hypertensive emergency). Tension headache: lifestyle + relaxation.
R51.referral: Meningitis signs, sudden severe headache, neurological signs, headache >1 week in adults, children >3 days.

R53.treatment: Malaise/fatigue: FBC, glucose, thyroid, HIV test. Treat underlying cause (anaemia, infection, hypothyroidism, depression). Lifestyle (sleep, exercise, diet).
R53.referral: Persistent >4 weeks, weight loss, fever, lymphadenopathy.

R73.treatment: Elevated blood glucose: lifestyle modification (diet, exercise, weight loss). If confirmed diabetes: Metformin 500mg daily, titrate. Repeat fasting glucose.

S00.treatment: Superficial head injury: clean wound, chlorhexidine 0.05%, dress. Tetanus toxoid if not immunised within 5y. Paracetamol for pain. Observe for concussion.
S00.referral: Loss of consciousness, vomiting, focal neurology, deep wound, suspected skull fracture.

S06.treatment: Intracranial injury: airway, breathing, circulation. Do NOT give sedatives unless intubated. IV Sodium chloride 0.9% if hypotensive. Urgent referral.

S52.treatment: Forearm fracture: immobilise with backslab/splint. Analgesia (Paracetamol + Ibuprofen, or Morphine if severe). Refer for X-ray and orthopaedic assessment.

S61.treatment: Hand wound: clean thoroughly, chlorhexidine 0.05%, dress. Antibiotics (Cefalexin 500mg 6 hourly × 5 days OR Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 875/125mg 12 hourly × 5 days). Tetanus toxoid. X-ray for foreign body/fracture.
S61.referral: All hand wounds — hand surgery referral.

S72.treatment: Femur fracture: immobilise (traction, splint). Morphine 5–10mg IM for pain. IV fluids if shock. Urgent referral.

S82.treatment: Lower leg fracture: immobilise with backslab. Analgesia. Elevate. Refer for X-ray and orthopaedic assessment. Assess for compartment syndrome (pain, pallor, paraesthesia, paralysis, pulselessness).
S82.referral: All cases — orthopaedic referral. Urgent if open fracture.

S93.treatment: Ankle sprain: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation. Paracetamol 1g 6 hourly + Ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly. Crutches if unable to weight bear. X-ray to exclude fracture (Ottawa rules).
S93.referral: Severe pain, unable to weight bear, suspected fracture, no improvement.

T14.treatment: Unspecified injury: assess mechanism, examine fully. Clean wounds, immobilise fractures, analgesia. Tetanus toxoid if not immunised within 5y.

T78.4.treatment: Allergy unspecified: Cetirizine 10mg daily (or Chlorphenamine 4mg 6–8 hourly). Avoid allergen. If anaphylaxis: Adrenaline 0.5mg IM, oxygen, IV fluids, hydrocortisone 200mg IV, promethazine 25mg IM.

Z00.0.treatment: General adult medical examination: BP, weight, BMI, glucose, HIV test, TB screen. Age-appropriate screening (cervical, breast, prostate). Lifestyle counselling. Vaccinations.

Z11.treatment: Screening for infectious diseases: HIV test, TB screen, STI screen, hepatitis B/C. Vaccinate if susceptible. Counselling.

Z21.treatment: Asymptomatic HIV: initiate TLD (TDF+3TC+DTG) once daily. Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis if CD4 <200. Viral load at 3 and 10 months, then annually. TB screen at every visit.

Z23.treatment: Immunisation: follow EPI schedule. BCG at birth, OPV, RV, Hexavalent (DTaP-IPV-HB-Hib), PCV, Measles/Rubella, Tdap. Catch-up doses for missed vaccines. Report AEFIs.

Z30.treatment: Contraceptive management: offer choice (COC, POP, DMPA, implant, IUCD, condoms). Screen for contraindications. Educate on correct use and side effects. Emergency contraception if needed.

Z34.treatment: Supervision of normal pregnancy: booking visit (bloods, BP, urine), monthly until 28 weeks, then 2-weekly to 36, then weekly. Folic acid 5mg daily (1st trimester), Ferrous sulfate + Calcium. Tdap between 26–34 weeks. Screen for HIV, syphilis, anaemia.

Z38.treatment: Liveborn infant: dry, warm, skin-to-skin. Vitamin K 1mg IM. Chloramphenicol 1% eye ointment. BCG + OPV0. Initiate breastfeeding within 1 hour. Apgar score.
Z38.referral: Any abnormality, prematurity, respiratory distress, jaundice.

Z71.treatment: Counselling: provide supportive counselling. Screen for depression, anxiety, substance use. Refer to social worker if needed.
Z71.referral: Severe mental health issues, abuse, suicidal ideation.

Z76.0.treatment: Issue of repeat prescription: review medicine list, adherence, side effects. Provide 28-day supply (or up to 6 months for stable chronic conditions). Book follow-up.
Z76.0.referral: Poor adherence, new symptoms, medicine side effects.
